environment.description: Same Flask application deployed on EC2 in a private subnet. Origin is fronted by a CloudFront distribution with a custom origin access configuration: the origin's security group ONLY allows inbound traffic from CloudFront managed prefix list (com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing). CloudFront behaviors require signed URLs using a trusted key group (RSA 2048-bit key, policy restricts to specific resource paths with 300s TTL). Additionally, CloudFront has a response headers policy (ID: 67f7725c-6f97-4210-82d7-5512b31e9d03 - SecurityHeadersPolicy) that injects Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'none'; style-src 'self' on ALL responses. The CloudFront distribution also has a cache behavior that strips query string parameters from the cache key forwarding configuration for /jobs/*/status paths (query strings are NOT forwarded to origin for status pages).

config.infrastructure: AWS EC2 t3.medium in private subnet, no public IP

cloudfront.signed_urls: Required - Trusted Key Group with RSA-2048, canned policy, 300s expiry

config.network: Private subnet, no IGW route, NAT for outbound only
config.redis: ElastiCache Redis 6.2 in same VPC, AUTH enabled
